key_insight: Simulations support improved vane-rheometry conversion relations, with the 24-arm fractal vane producing nearly axisymmetric yielding that better approximates circular Couette flow.
engineering_relevance: Better torque-to-stress and rotation-to-strain-rate conversions can improve rheological property measurements for viscoplastic materials.
method: Model Herschel–Bulkley fluids in vane-in-cup fixtures.
Use augmented Lagrangian finite elements in 2D and regularised finite volumes in 3D.
Compare 4-arm, 6-arm and 24-arm fractal vanes to refine conversion closures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive 2D and 3D simulations across effective parameters, examining flow kinematics, yielding patterns and limitations of existing conversion relations.
watch_item: Experimental validation and quantitative error reductions for the proposed closures are not reported in the abstract.
paper_title: Three-dimensional computational rheometry of viscoplastic fluids in vane-in-cup fixtures
